title: minimize-sdk-abi-drift-and-shed-legacy-params
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Reduce SDK surface drift and technical debt by performing coordinated dependency upgrades across Python, JS, and Go clients, removing deprecated API parameters, and applying performance-focused cleanup (bundle size, request path simplifications). Outcome should be a minimal-breaking change release with a clear migration path, automated compatibility tests, and a 10-15% token-cost improvement for common server-side patterns.

Scope:
- Upgrade core HTTP and serialization libraries (node: replace axios -> undici; python: bump requests -> httpx/async support where safe; go: tidy and pin net/http and proto deps).
- Remove deprecated request parameters (legacy retry_hint, client_version_override, legacy_token_format) from public surface; keep short-term backwards-compat shim for 90 days.
- Apply tree-shaking and bundle-splitting techniques for the browser/Node bundles; reduce shipped bytes.
- Tighten transitive dependency pins and add CI gates to prevent unwanted pulls.
- Publish migration guide, changelog, and automated codemods for common patterns.

Acceptance criteria:
1) All three clients pass compatibility matrix: 2.x and 3.x app integrations via e2e harness with pinned old params.
2) Deprecation shims log a single warning per-process and support 1x fallback hop for 90 days.
3) CI failure rate for dependency drift < 2% over 30d.
4) Benchmarked median tail latency for small-batch generation unchanged or improved; median token cost reduced by at least 10% under recommended settings.
5) Docs/migration guide live and linked from README and Console release notes.

Planned rollout: staged releases in three waves (node -> python -> go) with canaries and community beta.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Undici improves Node throughput but requires bumping supported Node baseline; will require communication to customers pinned to older runtimes.
- Removing legacy params risks breakage for some enterprise integrations; mitigation by shim and partner outreach.
- Pinning transitive deps reduces flexibility for emergent CVE patches; mitigation: scheduled monthly dep refresh plus emergency path.

Artifacts:
- Migration doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDKs/2026-SDK-Dep-Upgrades (draft)
- Compatibility harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-compat-harness/pulls/42 (WIP)
